record_type_quote: In this article, we report on our study that replicated a study of Hagger et al. (2006) in which Self-Determination Theory (SDT) and the Theory of Planned Behavior (TBP) are combined according Vallerand's (1997) explain the motivation sequence regarding DLMs usage by teachers.

targets.authors: Hagger M.S., Chatzisarantis N.L.D. & Harris J.
targets.title: From psychological need satisfaction to intentional behavior: Testing a motivational sequence in two behavioral contexts
targets.evidence_quote: Our study addressed the question whether Hagger's et al. model, in which SDT and TPB (i.e., IMBP) are combined using Vallerand's hierarchical model of motivation, will still be valid if this combined model is applied to teachers' use of Wikiwijs DLMs (rather than students performing exercising and dieting behavior).
targets.outcome_quote: The high contribution of attitude to the explanation of the variance in intention is also found by Hagger et al. (ibid) in both the exercising and dieting case (exercising = .264, p < .01; dieting = .548, p < .01). The low contribution of subjective norm is also found by Hagger et al. (ibid) in the exercising case (exercising = not given, non-significant) but not in the dieting case where the contribution was high (dieting = .207, p < .01). However, the low contribution of self-efficacy ( = .06, p < .05) to the explanation of the variance in intention is somewhat in contrast with the findings of Hagger et al. (ibid).
targets.outcome_reasoning: Authors explicitly contrast two structural relationships with the original while confirming others. Cautiously positive model applicability and largely supported findings do not assert complete replication.
